# Compute Correlations between Parameters

```{r}
library(data.table)
library(stringr)

# Ensure m1_posterior is a data.table
setDT(m1_posterior)

# Define the target parameter prefixes
target_prefixes <- c("time", "b_gain.p", "b_risk.p", "alpha.p", "bias", "theta.p")
pattern <- paste0("^(", paste(target_prefixes, collapse = "|"), ")\\[\\d+\\]$")

# Keep only relevant columns
target_cols <- grep(pattern, names(m1_posterior), value = TRUE)
filtered_dt <- m1_posterior[, ..target_cols]

# Step 1: Compute posterior means for each parameter
posterior_means <- filtered_dt[, lapply(.SD, mean), .SDcols = target_cols]

# Step 2: Convert to long format to extract participant IDs and metric names
long <- melt(posterior_means, variable.name = "metric", value.name = "mean_value")
long[, c("base_metric", "participant_id") := tstrsplit(metric, "\\[|\\]", perl = TRUE)]
long[, base_metric := gsub("\\.p", "", base_metric)]

# Step 3: Cast to wide format (one row per participant)
wide <- dcast(long, participant_id ~ base_metric, value.var = "mean_value")

# Step 4: Compute correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(wide[, -1, with = FALSE], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# View result
print(cor_matrix)
```


## Draw Posteriors for DDM Parameterse

### Group Level

```{r}
# Define the .mu variable patterns to group by
mu_variable_groups <- c("time.mu", "b_gain.mu", "b_risk.mu", "alpha.mu", "bias.mu", "theta.mu")

# Extract and compute summaries for .mu variables
group_level_summaries <- lapply(
  mu_variable_groups,
  function(mu_var) {
    # Extract the values for the .mu variable
    mu_values <- m1_posterior[[mu_var]]
    
    # Compute group-level summaries
    data.frame(
      variable_group = mu_var,
      mean = mean(mu_values),
      lower_95 = quantile(mu_values, 0.025),
      upper_95 = quantile(mu_values, 0.975),
      prob_positive = mean(mu_values > 0),
      prob_positive = mean(mu_values < 0),
      non_zero = quantile(mu_values, 0.025) > 0 | quantile(mu_values, 0.975) < 0
    )
  }
)

# Combine results into a single data frame
group_level_summaries <- do.call(rbind, group_level_summaries)

# Print results
print(group_level_summaries)
```

Drawing the posteriors:

```{r}
# Define the .mu variable patterns to group by
mu_variable_groups <- c("time.mu", "b_gain.mu", "b_risk.mu", "alpha.mu", "bias.mu", "theta.mu")

# Loop through each .mu variable and save the plot
for (mu_var in mu_variable_groups) {
  # Extract the posterior samples for the current variable
  mu_values <- m1_posterior[[mu_var]]
  
  # Calculate the mean of the posterior distribution
  mean_value <- mean(mu_values)
  
  # Create the plot
  png(
    filename = paste0("Figures/", mu_var, "_posterior_distribution.png"),
    width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300
  )
  
  # Plot the histogram
  hist(
    mu_values, 
    breaks = 50, 
    probability = TRUE, 
    main = paste("Posterior Distribution for", mu_var), 
    xlab = "Value", 
    ylab = "Density", 
    col = "#ADD8E6", 
    border = "#636363"
  )
  
  # Overlay the density curve
  lines(density(mu_values), col = "black", lwd = 2)
  
  # Add a dotted line at the mean
  abline(v = mean_value, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
  
  # Add a legend
  legend(
    "topright",
    legend = paste("Mean =", round(mean_value, 3)),
    col = "red",
    lty = 2,
    lwd = 2,
    bty = "n"
  )
  
  dev.off()
}
```


### Individualized

```{r}
library(furrr) # For parallel processing
plan(multisession) # Use multiple cores for parallel execution

# Define the variable patterns to group by
variable_groups <- c("time\\[", "b_gain\\.p\\[", "b_risk\\.p\\[", "alpha\\.p\\[", "bias\\[", "theta\\.p\\[")

col_names <- c("Time", "Gain Weight", "Risk Weight", "Alpha", "Bias", "Theta")

# Function to calculate individual summaries for a given variable group
compute_individual_summaries <- function(group_pattern) {
  # Find matching columns
  matching_columns <- grep(group_pattern, names(m1_posterior), value = TRUE)
  
  # Parallelized computation for each participant
  future_map_dfr(
    matching_columns,
    ~ {
      participant_values <- m1_posterior[[.x]]
      data.frame(
        variable_group = group_pattern,
        participant = .x,
        mean = mean(participant_values),
        lower_95 = quantile(participant_values, 0.025),
        upper_95 = quantile(participant_values, 0.975),
        prob_positive = mean(participant_values > 0),
        non_zero = quantile(participant_values, 0.025) > 0 | quantile(participant_values, 0.975) < 0
      )
    },
    .progress = TRUE # Show progress bar
  )
}

# Apply the function to all variable groups
individual_summaries <- future_map_dfr(variable_groups, compute_individual_summaries)

# Print final results
print(individual_summaries)

```

## Clean DDM Data

```{r}
# Extract DDM Metrics
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# Step 1: Identify columns with square brackets in m1_posterior
# Extract columns that match the pattern with ".p[XX]" or just "[XX]"
selected_columns <- m1_posterior %>%
  select(matches("\\[\\d+\\]$"))

# Step 2: Calculate the averages for each column
averages <- selected_columns %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean, na.rm = TRUE))

# Step 3: Extract both metric_name and participant_id, handling both ".p[XX]" and "[XX]"
column_info <- tibble(
  full_colname = colnames(averages),
  participant_id = str_extract(colnames(averages), "(?<=\\[)\\d+(?=\\])"),  # Extract participant ID if present in square brackets
  metric_name = str_replace(colnames(averages), "\\.?p?\\[\\d+\\]$", "")  # Remove either ".p[XX]" or "[XX]"
)

# Pivot the data into wide format where each metric_name becomes a separate column
averages_wide <- averages %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "full_colname", values_to = "average") %>%
  left_join(column_info, by = "full_colname") %>%
  mutate(participant_id = as.numeric(participant_id)) %>%
  select(participant_id, metric_name, average) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric_name, values_from = average)  # Pivot into wide format
```

# Ridge Regression

```{r}
compute_feature_importance <- function(data, response, predictors, 
         n_subsets = 100, subset_fraction = 1, feature_fraction = 0.8, 
         lambda = 0.1) {
  # List to store the importance scores for each subset
  feature_importance_list <- list()

  independent_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")))
  
  # Define the full design matrix to set column names
  full_matrix <- model.matrix(independent_formula, data = data)[, -1]
  all_columns <- colnames(full_matrix)
  
  # Compute feature frequencies
  feature_frequencies <- colMeans(full_matrix != 0)  # Proportion of non-zero values per feature
  
  for (i in 1:n_subsets) {
    # Randomly sample a subset of the data
    subset_data <- data %>%
      sample_frac(subset_fraction)
    
    # Prepare the design matrix for independent variables using the formula
    data_matrix <- model.matrix(independent_formula, data = subset_data)[, -1]  # Drop intercept column
    
    # Randomly sample a subset of the columns (features)
    selected_features <- sample(all_columns, size = floor(feature_fraction * length(all_columns)))
    data_matrix <- data_matrix[, selected_features, drop = FALSE]
    
    # Align with full column set, filling missing columns with 0
    missing_cols <- setdiff(all_columns, colnames(data_matrix))
    for (col in missing_cols) {
      data_matrix <- cbind(data_matrix, `col` = 0)
      colnames(data_matrix)[ncol(data_matrix)] <- col  # Assign correct column name
    }
    data_matrix <- data_matrix[, all_columns, drop = FALSE]  # Reorder to match full_matrix column order
    
    # Initialize feature importance matrix once we know the number of columns in data_matrix
    if (i == 1) {
      feature_importance <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_subsets, ncol = length(all_columns))
      colnames(feature_importance) <- all_columns
    }
    
    # Extract the response variable
    y <- subset_data[[response]]
    
    # Fit ridge regression (alpha = 0 for ridge)
    ridge_model <- glmnet(data_matrix, y, alpha = 0, lambda = lambda, standardize = TRUE)
    # Store absolute values of coefficients for the current subset
    coef_vector <- abs(as.vector(coef(ridge_model)[-1]))  # Drop intercept and convert to vector
    # coef_vector <- (as.vector(coef(ridge_model)[-1]))
    # Store the coefficients in the feature importance matrix
    feature_importance[i, ] <- coef_vector
  }
  
  # browser()
  
  # Compute the average importance score across subsets
  importance_scores <- colMeans(feature_importance, na.rm = TRUE)
  importance_se <- apply(feature_importance, 2, function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n_subsets))
  
   # Adjust importance scores by feature frequency
  adjusted_importance_scores <- importance_scores * feature_frequencies
  
  # Return a sorted dataframe with importance scores and standard errors
  importance_df <- data.frame(
    Feature = colnames(feature_importance),
    Importance = adjusted_importance_scores,
    StdError = importance_se
  )
  importance_df <- importance_df %>% arrange(desc(Importance))
  
  return(importance_df)
}

```

I will save these feature importance and coefficient results in the file, ridge_regression.RData

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(data.table)
library(glmnet)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1234)

column_names = colnames(final_table)

# Remove unwanted columns (explicitly removing 'X')
predictors <- column_names[
  !grepl("^(participant_id|user_id|rt|key_press|trial_index|time_elapsed|condition|condition_per_trial|total_trials|treatment_display|risk|gain|no_effect|experimental_treatment_selected|Progress|Duration..in.seconds.|RecordedDate|ResponseId|attention_check|Q1802|Income|Major|EmploymentStatus)", column_names) &
  column_names != "X" # Explicitly exclude the 'X' column
]

final_table <- final_table[complete.cases(final_table[, ..predictors])]
# final_table[, condition := relevel(factor(condition), ref = "Motor Function")]

# Define dependent and independent variables
dependent_vars <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")
predictors = setdiff(predictors, dependent_vars)

independent_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")))

# Prepare the design matrix for independent variables using the formula
data_matrix <- model.matrix(independent_formula, data = final_table)[, -1]  # Drop intercept column

# Standardize the response and predictors
coef_list <- list()
# List to store the importance data frames for each response variable
importance_results <- list()

for (dep_var in dependent_vars) {
  print(dep_var)
  # Standardize the dependent variable
  y <- scale(final_table[[dep_var]])

  # Perform cross-validated ridge regression
  cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(data_matrix, y, alpha = 0)  # Ridge regression (alpha = 0)
  best_lambda <- cv_fit$lambda.min
  ridge_model <- glmnet(data_matrix, y, alpha = 0, lambda = best_lambda)

  # Make predictions
  predictions <- predict(ridge_model, newx = data_matrix)
  
  # Calculate R-squared
  ss_total <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)  # Total sum of squares
  ss_residual <- sum((y - predictions)^2)  # Residual sum of squares
  r_squared <- 1 - (ss_residual / ss_total)
  
  # Convert R-squared to percentage
  percent_variance_explained <- r_squared * 100
  percent_variance_explained
  
  message <- sprintf("The model explains %.2f%% of the variance in the data.", percent_variance_explained)
  print(message)
  
  importance_df <- compute_feature_importance(data = final_table,
  response = dep_var,
  predictors = predictors,
  n_subsets = 100,
  lambda = best_lambda)
  
  importance_results[[dep_var]] <- importance_df

  # Extract coefficients, convert to data.table, and store standardized beta weights
  coefs <- as.data.table(as.matrix(coef(ridge_model)))
  setnames(coefs, "s0", dep_var)
  coefs[, Predictor := rownames(coef(ridge_model))]
  
  # Remove the intercept row
  coefs <- coefs[Predictor != "(Intercept)"]
  
  # Append to list
  coef_list[[dep_var]] <- coefs
}

# Combine all coefficients into one table
coefficients_table <- Reduce(function(dt1, dt2) merge(dt1, dt2, by = "Predictor", all = TRUE), coef_list)

# Melt the data.table for easier plotting
melted_coefs <- melt(coefficients_table, id.vars = "Predictor", variable.name = "Dependent_Variable", value.name = "Beta_Weight")
```

Plot Results

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Example plotting function for one dependent variable
plot_importance <- function(importance_df, dependent_var_name) {
  # Order by absolute importance to get top 50 values
  plot_data <- importance_df %>%
    mutate(AbsImportance = abs(Importance)) %>%
    arrange(desc(AbsImportance)) %>%
    head(50) %>%  # Keep only the top 50 by absolute importance
    arrange(Importance) %>%  # Reorder by actual importance for plotting
    select(-AbsImportance) %>%
    mutate(Type = ifelse(Importance >= 0, "Positive", "Negative")) %>%
    mutate(Feature = factor(Feature, levels = Feature)) # Preserve order for plotting
  
  # Create the plot
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Importance, y = Feature)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, aes(color = Type)) +  # Dot for the mean
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Importance - StdError, xmax = Importance + StdError),
                   height = 0.2, color = "black") +  # Horizontal error bars
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Negative" = "darkred", "Positive" = "darkblue")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
```

## Perform the join with question text

```{r}
# Define the column names you want to process
columns_to_process <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")

# Create a list to store the results
results_list <- list()

# Loop through each column name and process it
for (col_name in columns_to_process) {
  # Process each column
  importance_result <- importance_results[[col_name]] %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      colname = ifelse(
        Feature %in% question_text$colname,
        Feature,
        question_text$colname[which(startsWith(Feature, question_text$colname))[1]]
      ),
      colname = ifelse(is.na(colname), "", colname)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    # Perform the join
    left_join(question_text, by = c("colname" = "colname")) %>%
    # Replace unmatched features with an empty string
    mutate(text = ifelse(is.na(text), "", text))
  
  # Store the result in the list
  results_list[[col_name]] <- importance_result
}
```

## Run Permutation Test

For this permutation test, we will shuffle the importance values for all of the different questions, and then recompute cluster means. The null distribution will be the cluster mean of each region in question. 

```{r}
run_permutation_test <- function(data, feature_name) {
data_plt <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Category = sapply(Feature, get_category),
    StdError = StdError,
    Importance = Importance
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Importance))

set.seed(123) # Set seed for reproducibility

# Define the number of permutations
n_permutations <- 10000

# Initialize a dataframe to store results
results <- data.frame(Category = character(), P_Value = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Loop through each category in category_mapping
for (category_name in names(category_mapping)) {
  
  # Subset the Importance values for the given category
  category_importance <- data_plt$Importance[data_plt$Category == category_name]
  
  # Compute the observed mean
  test_mean <- mean(category_importance, na.rm = TRUE)
  test_sd <- sd(category_importance, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Generate the null distribution by shuffling Importance values
  null_distribution <- replicate(n_permutations, {
    shuffled_importance <- sample(data_plt$Importance)
    mean(shuffled_importance[data_plt$Category == category_name], na.rm = TRUE)
  })
  
  # Compute the p-value: proportion of times test_mean is greater than or equal to null_distribution
  p_value <- mean(test_mean >= null_distribution)
  
  # Store results in dataframe
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(Category = category_name, test_mean = test_mean, test_sd = test_sd,P_Value = p_value, 
      Null_Distribution = I(list(null_distribution))))
}

# Display results
return(results)
}


# Create plots for each measure
measures <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")

# Run the permutation test for each measure and store results as a named list
results <- setNames(lapply(measures, function(measure) {
  run_permutation_test(importance_results[[measure]], measure)
}), measures)
```


# Do the permutation test (OLD)

## Product of Importance and Valence

We will use the raw importance values and multiply it by the valence score

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(vader)  # Install the vader package for sentiment analysis

# Precompute valence scores for all dataframes in results_list
results_list <- lapply(results_list, function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(valence = vader_df(text)$compound)  # Precompute valence scores
  return(df)
})

# Function to compute total_valence_score using precomputed valence
compute_total_valence_score <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(score = Importance * valence) %>%
    summarize(total_valence_score = sum(score, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(total_valence_score)
}

compute_top10_valence_score <- function(df) {
  # Sort the dataframe by the desired column (e.g., Importance) in descending order
  df_top10 <- df %>%
    arrange(desc(Importance)) %>%  # Replace Importance with the column to sort by
    slice_head(n = 10)  # Select the top 10 rows
  
  # Compute the total_valence_score for the top 10 rows
  df_top10 %>%
    mutate(score = Importance * valence) %>%
    summarize(total_valence_score = sum(score, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(total_valence_score)
}

# Permutation test function
perform_permutation_test <- function(df, n_permutations = 1000) {
  # Compute the original total_valence_score
  original_score <- compute_total_valence_score(df)
  
  # Perform permutations
  permuted_scores <- replicate(n_permutations, {
    shuffled_df <- df %>%
      mutate(Importance = sample(Importance))  # Shuffle Importance values
    compute_total_valence_score(shuffled_df)
  })
  
  # Compute the probability that the original score is higher than permuted scores
  p_value <- mean(original_score > permuted_scores)
  
  list(
    original_score = original_score,
    p_value = p_value
  )
}

# Permutation test function
perform_permutation_test_top10 <- function(df, n_permutations = 1000) {
  # Compute the original total_valence_score
  original_score <- compute_top10_valence_score(df)
  
  # Perform permutations
  permuted_scores <- replicate(n_permutations, {
    shuffled_df <- df %>%
      mutate(Importance = sample(Importance))  # Shuffle Importance values
    compute_top10_valence_score(shuffled_df)
  })
  
  # Compute the probability that the original score is higher than permuted scores
  p_value <- mean(original_score > permuted_scores)
  
  list(
    original_score = original_score,
    p_value = p_value
  )
}

# Apply the permutation test to all dataframes in results_list
results_with_probabilities <- lapply(results_list, function(df) {
  perform_permutation_test(df)
})

results_with_probabilities_top10 <- lapply(results_list, function(df) {
  perform_permutation_test_top10(df)
})
```

## Product of rank and importance

```{r}
# Function to compute total_valence_score using rank * valence
compute_rank_valence_score <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(score = (NROW(df) - rank) * valence) %>%  # Compute score as rank * valence
    summarize(total_valence_score = sum(score, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(total_valence_score)
}

compute_top10_rank_valence_score <- function(df) {
  # Sort the dataframe by the desired column (e.g., Importance) in descending order
  df_top10 <- df %>%
    arrange(rank) %>%  # Replace Importance with the column to sort by
    slice_head(n = 10)  # Select the top 10 rows
  
  df_top10 %>%
    mutate(score = (NROW(df) - rank) * valence) %>%  # Compute score as rank * valence
    summarize(total_valence_score = sum(score, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(total_valence_score)
}

# Permutation test with shuffled ranks
perform_rank_permutation_test <- function(df, n_permutations = 1000) {
  df = df %>%
    mutate(rank = row_number())  # Assign rank based on row number
  # Compute the original total_valence_score
  original_score <- compute_rank_valence_score(df)
  
  # Perform permutations
  permuted_scores <- replicate(n_permutations, {
    shuffled_df <- df %>%
      mutate(rank = sample(row_number()))  # Shuffle row numbers
    compute_rank_valence_score(shuffled_df)
  })
  
  # Compute the probability that the original score is higher than permuted scores
  p_value <- mean(original_score > permuted_scores)
  
  list(
    original_score = original_score,
    p_value = p_value
  )
}

perform_rank_permutation_test_top10 <- function(df, n_permutations = 1000) {
  df = df %>%
    mutate(rank = row_number())  # Assign rank based on row number
  # Compute the original total_valence_score
  original_score <- compute_top10_rank_valence_score(df)
  
  # Perform permutations
  permuted_scores <- replicate(n_permutations, {
    shuffled_df <- df %>%
      mutate(rank = sample(row_number()))  # Shuffle row numbers
    compute_top10_rank_valence_score(shuffled_df)
  })
  
  # Compute the probability that the original score is higher than permuted scores
  p_value <- mean(original_score > permuted_scores)
  
  list(
    original_score = original_score,
    p_value = p_value
  )
}

# Apply the rank-based permutation test to all dataframes in results_list
results_with_rank_probabilities <- lapply(results_list, function(df) {
  perform_rank_permutation_test(df)
})

results_with_rank_probabilities_top10 <- lapply(results_list, function(df) {
  perform_rank_permutation_test_top10(df)
})
```

# Summary Statistics

# NEW Regression Analysis

This new regression analysis runs many different regressions in a loop so that all coefficients
and p-values can be extracted efficiently.

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)

# Define dependent and independent variables
dependent_vars <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")
independent_vars <- c("condition", "GRIPS", "consequentalism", "politics", 
                      "Harm", "Fairness", "Loyalty", "Authority", "Sanctity", 
                      "sex", "poly(age, 2, raw=TRUE)", "BerlinScore", "ReligiousFactor")

# Initialize an empty data frame to store the results
results <- data.frame(Independent_Var = character(), 
                      Dependent_Var = character(),
                      Beta = numeric(), 
                      P_Value = numeric(), 
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Loop through each dependent variable
for(dep_var in dependent_vars) {
  # Loop through each independent variable
  for(ind_var in independent_vars) {
    # Create the formula
    formula <- as.formula(paste(dep_var, "~", ind_var))
    
    # Run the linear regression
    model <- lm(formula, data = final_table)
    
    # Extract the beta coefficient and p-value (ignoring intercept)
    summary_model <- summary(model)
    coef_data <- summary_model$coefficients
    
    # Check if independent variable has multiple levels (for factors)
    ind_var_rows <- grep(ind_var, rownames(coef_data))
    
    # Extract beta coefficient(s) and p-value(s) for the independent variable
    for(i in ind_var_rows) {
      beta <- coef_data[i, "Estimate"]
      p_value <- coef_data[i, "Pr(>|t|)"]
      t_value <- coef_data[i, "t value"]
      
      # Store the results in the results data frame
      results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
        Independent_Var = rownames(coef_data)[i],
        Dependent_Var = dep_var,
        Beta = beta,
        P_Value = p_value,
        T_Value = t_value
      ))
    }
  }
}

# Print or inspect the results
print(results)
```

```{r}
save(results, file='final_ddm_regression_results.RData')
```
